data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached at different nodes along the stem, alternating sides)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced out along the stem rather than crowded together)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (leaves are composed of multiple distinct leaflets attached to a central axis)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (each leaf has a terminal leaflet at the apex of the rachis)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 5 (multiple leaves clearly show three leaflets, while others show five leaflets)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): subopposite (leaflets along the rachis appear paired but with slight offsets)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (leaf margins are smooth with no teeth or serrations, though some leaves have holes)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (leaflets are broadly oval, widest near the middle)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (leaf tips come to a distinct, sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (leaf bases appear smooth and curved without a notch)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib runs the length of the leaflet with secondary veins branching off)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, fine, and spaced closely along the midrib
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (leaf surfaces reflect light, indicating a smooth texture)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no hairs are visible on the leaf surfaces)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): long (petioles are slender and extend a significant distance from the stem)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the stem is green, thin, and flexible, typical of a young seedling)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem appears smooth)
    19. Stem color: green (the stem is a uniform bright green)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no ridges or lenticels are visible on the stem)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex is visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint-like structure is visible at the leaf base)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils are present)
F. Notes: Some leaflets show irregular holes along the margins and in the center of the blade.
